name: יְהוֹאָחָז
summary: Jehoahaz son of Jehu, king of Israel, who did evil, so that Yahweh gave Israel into the hand of Hazael; he entreated Yahweh, and Yahweh gave Israel a saviour (2Ki 10:35; 13:1–9). Jehoahaz son of Josiah, king of Judah, whom the people anointed after Josiah's death and Pharaoh Neco bound at Riblah and carried to Egypt after three months, where he died (2Ki 23:30–34; 2Ch 36:1–4); Jeremiah calls him Shallum (Jer 22:11). Ahaziah of Judah is also called Jehoahaz (2Ch 21:17), and in the short spelling יוֹאָחָז the father of Joah the recorder under Josiah (2Ch 34:8). The name is יְהוֹ with the verb אָחַז, “Yahweh has taken hold”, the same two parts as אֲחַזְיָהוּ in the other order; scripture does not explain it.

evidence.note: “Jehu slept with his fathers … and Jehoahaz (יְהוֹאָחָז) his son reigned in his place.”
“Jehoahaz entreated the face of Yahweh, and Yahweh listened to him … and Yahweh gave Israel a saviour.”
“The people of the land took Jehoahaz son of Josiah and anointed him and made him king in place of his father.”
He reigned three months; Pharaoh Neco bound him at Riblah, and he came to Egypt and died there.
“Shallum son of Josiah … who went out from this place: he shall not return here any more.”
Of Jehoram's sons none was left “except Jehoahaz, the youngest”, the Ahaziah of 2Ch 22:1.

note: Takes e.az.ah (יְהוֹאָחָז) and e.az.be (יוֹאָחָז), which BDB files under הוה, the root of the divine name, like the other Jeho- names; the name's own root is this one. Token counts not checked beyond db lexicon-support. TIPNR lists the יוֹאָחָז spelling under both kings named Jehoahaz (2Ki 14:1 of Jehu's son) and keys the recorder's father as Joahaz@2Ch.34.8.
